A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuralNDCG-based alignment work, renamed from OPO to PPA. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing retained material to be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen2-0.5B and Mistral-7B experiments, benchmark comparisons, ablations, simulations and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds Llama3.1-8B evaluations, human ratings, rank-flip analyses and computational measurements.

M1.justification: OPO and PPA use the same reference-relative reward scores, NeuralSort relaxation, Sinkhorn scaling and NeuralNDCG objective; the ApproxNDCG alternative is also retained. Renaming, added pseudocode and discount-function ablations do not establish a change to the proposed training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Arena-Hard evaluation in Appendix Table 13. UltraChat200k, ListUltraFeedback, AlpacaEval and MT-Bench remain, preserving the original broad conversational preference-alignment task while modestly extending benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: RankNet is added alongside existing comparators in the Qwen2 comparison (v2 Table 1) and Mistral comparison (Table 12). Others vs Worst is added to the Mistral comparisons in Tables 11–12. LiPO and LambdaRank represent the retained comparator, despite naming and classification changes.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama3.1-8B configurations, training-step rank-flip evaluation, a human study with 20 raters judging 300 pairs, and a timing test using 10,000 lists. Existing dataset splits and judge pipelines remain. The revised reference-model description says Instruct versions, while the Mistral table still specifies Zephyr-7B-SFT, leaving an actual Mistral setting change unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of successful rank flips and reference-model dependence (Figure 2), surrogate gradients (Figures 6–7), alternative discount functions (Table 2), and sorting overhead (Appendix H). Existing sensitivity and response examples largely remain, but the beta=0.05 component-ablation results from v1 Table 4 are omitted.

E5.justification: Both training tables specify random seed 42. Neither version reports repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, standard errors or formal significance tests. The new human-study sample counts and rank-flip distributions do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds model, baseline, human-rating, rank-flip, gradient, discount and timing results while retaining the original benchmark scores. Table 4 reports human win rates of 68%, 55% and 54%; Table 13 shows PPA below All Pairs on Arena-Hard, 60.17 versus 61.64. Reporting inconsistencies accompany these additions: Table 4 labels automatic scores as versus SFT that Figures 3 and 8 assign to Single Pair, and Table 1 gives ApproxNDCG an average of 59.33 although its four entries average 58.54.

T1.justification: New Section 5 and Appendix B introduce an optimal-ranking property, a DPO loss-threshold counterexample, formal ranking-accuracy and successful-flip definitions, and a probabilistic rank-flip proposition with proofs. Appendix G also corrects the ApproxNDCG ratio algebra, replacing the erroneous exponential-factor expression in v1 Equation 19 with a ratio raised to alpha times beta in v2 Equation 23.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion newly emphasize Bradley-Terry ranking limitations, superior ranking accuracy and a theoretical explanation. These replace the earlier prominence of expanding the negative-sample pool as a central contribution. The NDCG-based alignment proposal and general benchmark-advantage claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations based on rank-flip efficiency, objective differences, gradient behavior and agreement between human and automatic judgments. It reframes the negative-sampling findings around list size versus comparison count. The acknowledged absence of theoretical analysis is removed, while the limitation concerning reward models' imperfect correspondence to human preferences remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds NeuralSort pseudocode and worked matrices, specifies 50 Sinkhorn iterations for the timing experiment, and extends training documentation to Llama3.1-8B. It updates the dataset access link and omits v1's code-repository footnote. These are documentation and access-instruction changes, without evidence that the underlying method changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. (2024) on preference-ranking failures and FocalPO (2025), connecting them to its ranking-based motivation. Several earlier citations, including the contrastive-learning reference, disappear. Most pairwise, listwise and learning-to-rank coverage is retained, with the detailed survey moved to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The title, method terminology, abstract, introduction and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. Related work moves near the beginning with expanded material in Appendix A; NeuralSort details move into Appendix D. The appendices are reorganized, and the former discussion becomes a conclusion with separate limitations.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the workflow to show NeuralSort explicitly, relocates major tables and restructures the ablation display. It adds rank-flip and gradient figures and human, model and timing tables. The former NeuralNDCG approximation-error panel is removed, and retained graphics are resized, relabeled or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful empirical evaluations and implementation guidance, but introduces substantive reliability problems. Appendix B.3's Gaussian-CDF inequality following Equation 11 does not follow for negative integration values, undermining a newly central theoretical claim. Table 4 also has unexplained SFT versus Single Pair comparator labeling. These problems coexist with the empirical and documentation gains, preventing a confident judgment of the net quality change.
